topic: Decoding Wordle: Using Information Theory to Win

sections.title: Introduction: The Guessing Game
lecture_lines: Wordle is a game of uncertainty.
We want to minimize our guesses.
We do this by maximizing information gain.
animations: Display Title: "Introduction: The Guessing Game" in #FFFFFF.
Fade in a box containing 16 hidden items.
Demonstrate searching sequentially through the 16 items.
Highlight the inefficiency of sequential guessing.
Transition to the concept of binary reduction.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Uncertainty with Entropy
lecture_lines: Entropy measures uncertainty in a system.
It shows how information is distributed.
Think of it as probability branches.
animations: Define Entropy H(S) using a standard math formula in #FFFF00.
Visualize entropy as a measure of disorder/uncertainty.
Show how entropy decreases as we gain information.

sections.title: The Core Logic: Information Gain
lecture_lines: Choose words to split pools equally.
Information gain reveals the answer faster.
animations: Define Information Gain as reduction in entropy.
Formula: Gain(S, A) = H(S) - H(S|A) in #00FF00.
Demonstrate how a split reduces entropy on example.
Show tree nodes updating with gain values.

sections.title: Application: The Strategy in Action
lecture_lines: Repeat until the word is found.
animations: Select attribute with highest Information Gain.
Visualize splitting the data into two subsets.

sections.title: Conclusion: Summary and Intuition
lecture_lines: Wordle is about reducing information state.
animations: Summarize key takeaway: Entropy measures uncertainty.
Summarize: Information Gain drives the split decision.
Final screen: Visualize the full Decision Tree structure.
